newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais says Russia to raise extra 30 trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Chubais says Russia to raise extra 30 trln rbls.

text.p: Russia plans to raise 30 trillion roubles of extra cash for the state budget and will use the money to repay debts in the social sector, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.
Chubais told a meeting of Siberian leaders that the money would be raised with a "new approach to operations on the security market" and by reclaiming debts owed to Moscow by other countries.
He gave no details, but Russia is owed billions of dollars both by countries lent money by the Soviet Union and by former Soviet republics which owe money for energy supplies.
"With the help of this we can solve or ease the sharpest problems in our budget crisis," Chubais said.
Chubais said the largest debts were for pensions, for public sector workers and in the housing sector.
Pensioners were owed 12.5 trillion roubles, public sector workers were owed 14 trillion roubles and the debts of the housing sector were also 14 trillion roubles.
The government, unable to fulfil its ambitious budget, is about to propose new spending plans for 1997, cutting spending across the board.

The State Duma lower house of parliament is due to debate the sequestration plans on May 21, but communist deputies have already served notice that they will oppose the proposals. Some want the government to print money to fund the budget shortfall, something ruled out by the reformist government.
